description.value: A behavioural and voxel-based morphometry study of altered auditory hedonic responses in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and Alzheimer's disease.

spans.text: Here we addressed this issue in a cohort of 73 patients representing major canonical dementia syndromes (behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), semantic dementia (SD), progressive nonfluent aphasia (PNFA) amnestic Alzheimer's disease (AD)) using a semi-structured caregiver behavioural questionnaire and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of patients' brain MR images.

value: we hypothesised that these neurodegenerative syndromes would produce a complex of auditory hedonic abnormalities with bi-directional shifts in the valuation of particular sound categories (environmental sound and music); and that such abnormalities would be more common in the syndromes of bvFTD and SD than other neurodegenerative syndromes, and would correlate with altered sweet food preference.

We further hypothesised that altered auditory hedonic responsiveness would be associated with grey matter changes in a distributed brain network including areas previously implicated in encoding the affective salience of sounds and other sensory signals (in particular, insula and anterior cingulate cortex: ), evaluating their affective meaning (in particular, antero-mesial temporal lobe: ) and representing their reward value (in particular, ventral striatum: ).

spans.text: Based on previous clinical evidence, we hypothesised that these neurodegenerative syndromes would produce a complex of auditory hedonic abnormalities with bi-directional shifts in the valuation of particular sound categories (environmental sound and music); and that such abnormalities would be more common in the syndromes of bvFTD and SD than other neurodegenerative syndromes, and would correlate with altered sweet food preference.
